subject: Re: Redwood model fit eval — next steps & parity thresholds
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-28T16:10:00Z
Subject: Model fit eval — post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Alex — great meeting today, thanks for walking us through the PayGrid routing & reconciliation flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Goal: validate parity (or acceptable degradation) between your internal routing model and open-source candidates for inference on production workloads. Primary KPI is intent-classification F1 and end-to-end routing accuracy on the 10k sample evaluation set you shared.
- Recommended models to include in the first run: Llama-2-Chat-13B (8-bit quant), Mistral-Instruct-7B (float16), RedPajama-INCITE-7B (8-bit). As a baseline we’ll also run your PayGrid proprietary model as the reference (you provided hashes on the call).
- Acceptance thresholds (proposal): parity = within 2-3 absolute F1 points on intent classification OR >= 90% acceptance on manual review for top-3 critical intents. If we see >3% drop, we’ll flag for prompt engineering / small finetune options. See attached parity_thresholds.xlsx for a suggested table.
- Deliverables from PayGrid: upload the 10k labeled sample to the Drive link (or send a secure S3 link), confirm the canonical prompt set (attached paygrid_eval_prompt_set_v1.json), and list any PII-scrubbing rules we should apply.
- Deliverables from Redwood: we’ll run the benchmark across the recommended open models + your baseline on Redwood Dedicated infra, provide the full quantitative report (latency, per-intent F1, rejection rate) and a short human review summary by EoD next Wednesday (2026-04-01). Estimated cost for the run is in the Drive link; we can apply a one-time evaluation credit if needed.

Next steps: can you confirm (1) dataset upload + location, (2) whether we should include the larger 30B open models or stick to the 7–13B family for this pass, and (3) any compliance requirements for the evaluation infra (e.g., must be run in US-only region)?

Thanks — looking forward to getting you a clean parity readout.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: paygrid_eval_prompt_set_v1.json, parity_thresholds.xlsx, paygrid_benchmark_report_q1.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-29T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Model fit eval — post-demo recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — that recap is perfect. Quick answers:

1) I’ll upload the 10k sample to the Drive folder by EOD today. We’ll include the canonical labels for the 12 routing intents and the edge-case subset for chargeback flows.
2) For this first pass please stick to the 7–13B family. If we see promising results we can expand to 30B candidates in phase 2.
3) US-only is required for this dataset (PCI-adjacent). Please run the eval in the us-east region and confirm access controls.

One ask: can we get a short summary of what parity means operationally? Our product team will need a clear go/no-go definition. Happy to sync on a 15-min call if helpful.

—
Alex Johnson
Product Lead, ML | PayGrid
alex.johnson@paygrid.com | (617) 555-4433

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-29T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Model fit eval — post-demo recap & next steps

Hey Alex — quick technical follow-up on parity and eval logistics:

- Parity operational definition (short): if an open-model configuration achieves intent-level F1 within 2 absolute points of your proprietary baseline across the prioritized intent set AND median latency < 1.5x of baseline with the same cost envelope, we classify it as "parity-acceptable" for an initial rollout. If F1 gap is 2–5 points, we flag for prompt engineering + targeted distillation; >5 points requires more substantial finetune. Manual review acceptance (>=90%) is used as a safety threshold for the most critical intents.

- Eval infra notes: we will run all evals in us-east on a dedicated job queue (isolated VPC). We’ll apply your PII-scrubbing rules before any storage. Results will include per-intent precision/recall/F1, token-level latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and human-review pass rates for the critical subset.

- Prompts & temperature: we’ll run with the canonical prompts attached (paygrid_eval_prompt_set_v1.json) and three temperature/settings buckets (deterministic: temp=0.0; default: temp=0.3; explorative: temp=0.7). We’ll track changes in hallucination rate for downstream reconciliation fields.

- Timeline & cost: the job for the 10k sample across three models should complete within 48 hours once the data is available. Estimated compute cost ~ $700–1,200 depending on batching/quantization. Marissa — can you confirm if we should bill this to the evaluation credit or push to the committed contract?

If helpful, I can post a lightweight notebook with the eval commands and metric extraction for your engineers.

—
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-30T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Model fit eval — post-demo recap & next steps

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick turnaround.

Next steps from here:
- Alex: confirm when the Drive upload is complete (we’ll pull and validate access) and confirm billing preference (apply eval credit vs bill).
- Aditya/Dev: please queue the evaluation jobs (us-east) once upload is confirmed and share the run notebook with PayGrid engineers.
- Marissa: I’ll schedule a 30-min results review for Thursday 2026-04-02 10:00 AM ET; if that doesn’t work for your team let me know.

One operational note: if we observe a systematic regression on reconciliation numeric fields (even if intent parity looks good) we’ll highlight as a blocker — those regressions are frequently higher-impact than intent drop and may require small finetunes or hybrid routing rules. We’ll call that out in the report.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
